items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Piron's band, I mentioned that before -- it was impossible for you to get in that band.

ctx.x: Yeah, but it's finer than a Palm Beach. It's a Bangkok. My Dad had one. A Palm Beach is just white, white straw like. But this is a silk straw, like shiny. Very small! Very-very-very-very small. I gave (?) a Panama. So... Well, you get what you want.

So when you're playing music, you wait your time. You know, you say, well, you bide your time. Because here in New Orleans they had bands, and it was impossible for you to get in one of them bands. It was a family band. Piron's band, I mentioned that before -- it was impossible for you to get in that band. And you want to advance when you're playing music.

So they had Fate's band. Everybody looked at Fate Marable with awe, because he played that calliope on that boat, and he had a helluva band. That's the band that Louis Armstrong got his finishing touches [tetches], under the tutelage of David Jones. David Jones was a great reading musician. He helped Louis with his parts. He spent hours with Louis.
